content:
mina: quick heads-up — ran a small experiment this morning comparing current microbatch=8 policy vs dynamic-sampling for prefill-heavy workloads. p95 dropped, but p99 got worse on long-context requests.
raj: details? sample sizes, model, region?
mina: gptx-13b quantized fp16, 1k requests, 95th and 99th measured across 5-minute windows. dynamic-sampling means we greedily reduce per-worker microbatch when active queue depth>12 and fall back otherwise.
ashley: can you paste the flamegraph/profiler output?
mina: pasted below — note these are aggregated across workers:
```
prefill: 62%
decode: 28%
kernel-switching/overhead: 6%
queueing/synchronization: 4%
```
raj: interesting — prefill dominating. Does dynamic-sampling shift work to prefill or improve decode?
mina: dynamic reduced overall latency for short-context (<=512) by ~18% p95, but for 2048 tokens we see p99 regress ~9% — suspected KV cache misses and extra kernel selection churn.
dave: did you capture KV cache hit rate per request?
mina: yes — hit rate drops from 97% to 91% for long contexts under dynamic because smaller microbatches increase probability of partial KV state eviction across scheduling slots.
perf-bot: CI perf test 1772000400: kernel-switch-count increased by 22% vs baseline.
nashley: so smaller microbatches help latency for many requests but increase tail for long ones due to cache thrash + kernel switches. two knobs: cap microbatch for short requests only OR prefer sticky scheduling for requests with large prefill.
raj: what about prefill vs decode breakdown per sequence length?
mina: aggregated: for 128 tokens prefill ~40%, decode ~52%. for 2048 prefill ~78%, decode ~18%. So prefill scales worse with context, unsurprising.
dave: could we delay kernel-switch heuristic until after prefill finishes? e.g., avoid kernel-switching mid-request by pinning a kernel once prefill begins.
raj: that might help tail. downside: less optimal kernel for decode phase if different sequence shapes. But reducing mid-request switches could cut out that extra 6% overhead.
mina: also saw expensive cudaMemcpy bursts when microbatches are tiny — extra host<->device overhead.
nashley: propose experiment: 1) sticky-kernel per-request, 2) preferential-batching short-context in separate queue, 3) KV-cache LRU window increase for jobs with >1024 context. Run A/B for 2 hours.
dave: add metric: kernel-switch-count, kv-hit-rate, device memcpy-time, and request-context-length bucketed p95/p99. Also track throughput (tokens/s) to see tradeoff.
mina: I'll kick off the run. Quick config draft:
```json
{
  "scheduler": "dual-queue",
  "short_queue_threshold": 512,
  "microbatch_cap_short": 4,
  "microbatch_cap_long": 12,
  "sticky_kernel": true,
  "kv_lru_extend_ms": 120000
}
```
raj: one more thought — for long-context tails maybe we should pre-warm KV cache for frequent users by keeping recent prefixes pinned for ~5m. Could be cheaper than LRU window blowout.
mina: noted. will enable sticky_kernel + dual-queue first. schedule A/B against current policy (microbatch=8) and report back in ~3h.
nashley: please tag perf-bot when results are in. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: scheduled perf run 1772000460 (AB test) — notify:results -> #eng-runtime.
mina: thanks team. will post summary + graphs when complete.
